correctness.rationale: The normalized quadratic numerator of ω has conjugate roots α=(1+i√3)/6 and its conjugate, both of modulus 1/3; the normalized denominator is the product (1-αz)(1-conj(α)z). Thus ω is a degree-three Blaschke product fixing zero. With x=cos θ, the boundary real part of Φ equals (2/9)[3(1+x)²-2x³], strictly positive on [-1,1]; the harmonic minimum principle gives positivity on the disk. The odd exponential part u has zu'/u=P_e and is starlike, and the parity integral gives zf'/u=P, so the normalized f is close-to-convex and univalent. Independent exact multiplication of f'=P·(u/z), then integration and a permutation expansion of the determinant, gives (b2,b3,b4,b5)=(1/18,-71/486,11161/52488,55297/472392), H=-173595619/2754990144, and the two exact positive gaps as submitted. The two cited articles differ in ambient notation (2025 uses normalized univalent S, 2026 uses normalized analytic A), but the witness is in the smaller S and satisfies their matching subordination, so both contradictions follow. In fact positivity and the odd-part argument give univalence for the analytic class with this relation.
residual_risks: No claim about the sharp supremum or the precise origin of the erroneous 2026 bound. One line in the 2025 proof extraction appears to have the opposite sign on a3a5; the published determinant definition, which fixes the convention, is decisive.
